status_note: Reproduces on 55.0.0, the latest release, which fails where 51.0.0 gave a wrong date. No open issue: #25129 and #25432 (closed) fixed other `date_trunc` paths. Main not checked.
title: `date_trunc` to a month fails on a microsecond timestamp outside ±2⁶³ ns
summary: `date_trunc` to a week, month, quarter or year computes in nanoseconds, so a `Timestamp(Microsecond)` outside ±2⁶³ ns (before 1677 or after 2262) gives a wrong date on 51.0.0 and an error on 55.0.0, though Arrow represents it. Timestamp literals are cast to nanoseconds and fail there too.
repro: `select date_trunc('month', arrow_cast('2300-06-15T00:00:00', 'Timestamp(Microsecond, None)'))` gives `1715-11-01` on 51.0.0 and `Timestamp 10428048000000000 out of range` on 55.0.0; `date_part('year', …)` of it is `2300`.
`select cast('2300-06-15 00:00:00' as timestamp)` fails: `Overflow converting 2300-06-15 00:00:00 to Nanosecond`.
handling: The reference follows DataFusion here (`core/Sverify/Core/Time.lean`): calendar functions are defined within ±2⁶³ ns on every engine. A proposal to use 0001–9999 and refuse only on DataFusion is under review.
found_by: audit of DataFusion's limits on the shared path (2026-11-08)
